claims.statement: A Polish guarantee of origin is the legally designated proof to the final customer of renewable origin and does not itself confer property rights or physical electricity delivery.
Guarantees are electronic, unique, time-limited instruments whose transfer and cancellation are supervised through designated registry systems.
TGE issues final-customer confirmation on request of the seller-owner and now provides bulk transaction handling and a marketplace within the registry.
Axpo says it serves nearly 40000 Polish SMEs with renewable-origin coverage and introduced that coverage without additional or hidden charges.
Energa's current terms already pool GO purchase and cancellation across participating customers.
These incumbent and registry features make 800-2000 PLN per month for ordinary SME procurement evidence implausible without a distinct supply-chain audit requirement.
Poland had a national GO system but was not connected to the AIB Hub in the reviewed report, and AIB gave no membership timeline.
EU consumer law requires environmental claims to be specific and supportable and prohibits overstatement from one attribute to an entire product or business.
A non-custodial reconciliation layer may be lawful, but the reviewed evidence does not resolve Polish licensing, registry-account, mandate, or API access for the exact operating model.
The founder can build the data layer part-time and within available capital, but partner access and willingness to pay are not validated.

contrary_evidence: Large suppliers already bundle or collectively cancel GOs for SMEs.
Axpo explicitly describes renewable-origin coverage without extra charges.
TGE now has bulk transaction processing and a marketplace.
GOs are evidentiary attributes, not physical-delivery or ownership rights.
Poland's lack of AIB Hub connection limits assumed European interoperability.
Specific green claims remain subject to accuracy and anti-overstatement rules.
